title: Enrollment, Qualifying Inspection and Activation of HVAC Maintenance Agreements
content:
An HVAC Maintenance Agreement is enrolled on the customer's statement of the equipment, inspected by a network contractor, and activated only on a passed inspection within the inspection window.

## 1. Equipment and number of systems at enrollment

The equipment types and number of systems are taken from the customer's statement and must satisfy the entry gate and maximum systems of the agreement level. The entry gate of every Bridgewell Comfort Care level admits central air conditioners, heat pumps, gas furnaces and ductless mini-splits and requires a passed qualifying inspection. A ductless system counts as one system for up to the level's figure of ductless indoor heads per system.

The equipment is recorded as the customer describes it, for the property address the customer gives; at enrollment the customer's statement is the authority for the equipment types and the number of systems.

## 2. Length of a term

Each term lasts 12 calendar months, ending the day before the same calendar day 12 months later (the last day of the month when that day does not exist).

*Hypothetical example:* an agreement enrolled on 15 March has a first term ending on 14 March of the following year.

## 3. Qualifying inspection and activation

A network contractor performs a qualifying inspection. Its result is either passed or failed, repair needed.

An agreement is activated only when the qualifying inspection result is passed and the inspection was completed no later than 30 calendar days after the agreement is enrolled, counting from the day after the start date with the boundary day included.

The start date, the inspection date and the inspection result are read from the company's agreement record. Stated as conditions, activation requires both:

| Condition | Must be |
|---|---|
| Qualifying inspection result | passed |
| Inspection date | no later than the 30th calendar day, counting the day after the start date as day 1 |

### Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Start date | Inspection date and result | Day number of the inspection | Activation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 31 March, passed | 30 | Within the window; the agreement is activated |
| 1 March | 1 April, passed | 31 | Outside the window; not activated |
| 1 March | 20 March, failed, repair needed | 19 | Result not passed; not activated |

## 4. Failed inspection or no inspection in time

When the result is failed, repair needed, or no inspection is completed in that window, the enrollment is cancelled and, when the level's full refund on inspection failure applies (it applies on every Bridgewell Comfort Care level), every fee paid is credited and refunded; the customer may re-enroll after the repair.

## 5. Re-enrollment after expiry

A property re-enrolled no later than 30 calendar days (the late renewal grace period) after its previous agreement expired carries over that agreement's passed inspection result and inspection date and needs no new inspection.

*Hypothetical example:* an agreement whose term ended on 30 June expired at the end of that day. A re-enrollment of the property on 30 July is 30 days after expiry and carries over the earlier passed result and inspection date; a re-enrollment on 31 July is 31 days after and does not.

## Status of the agreement through these stages

An enrolled agreement becomes active when the agent activates it after a passed inspection; it becomes cancelled when the equipment fails the qualifying inspection or no inspection is completed in time.
